statecomptroller.seat: Comptroller of the State of New York
bio: Thomas P. DiNapoli is the State Comptroller, elected statewide.
The state’s chief fiscal officer. Audits state and local governments, and is the sole trustee of the state pension fund.
Appointed Comptroller by the Legislature in February 2007 and first elected in 2010. Statewide offices carry four year terms, with no term limit.
Kathy Hochul is the Governor, elected statewide.
Chief executive of the state. Proposes the state budget, signs or vetoes legislation, and appoints the heads of state agencies.
Became Governor in August 2021 on the resignation of her predecessor, and was elected to a full term in 2022. Statewide offices carry four year terms, with no term limit.
Antonio Delgado is the Lieutenant Governor, elected statewide on a ticket with the Governor.
Second in line to the Governor and president of the State Senate. Succeeds the Governor if the office falls vacant.
Appointed Lieutenant Governor in May 2022 and elected with the Governor in 2022. Statewide offices carry four year terms, with no term limit.
Letitia James is the Attorney General, elected statewide.
The state’s chief legal officer. Represents the state in court, enforces state law against fraud and abuse, and runs the Department of Law.
First elected in 2018 and sworn in January 2019. Statewide offices carry four year terms, with no term limit.

background: Served 14 years on the Hamburg Town Board; earlier worked as a legislative aide to Rep. John LaFalce and Sen. Daniel Patrick Moynihan.
Erie County Clerk, 2007 to 2011; won a 2011 special election to the U.S. House and lost the 2012 race in the redrawn 27th District.
Was Andrew Cuomo's running mate in 2014 and was elected Lieutenant Governor twice.
Sworn in as New York's 57th Governor on August 24, 2021.
positions: Says her administration delivered the largest middle-class tax rate cut in 70 years.
https://www.wcax.com/2026/10/14/hochul-blakeman-face-off-new-york-gubernatorial-debate/
Points to more than $10 billion in energy, inflation and other rebates to help residents with bills.
https://www.wcax.com/2026/10/14/hochul-blakeman-face-off-new-york-gubernatorial-debate/
Proposed moving toward universal child care for children under 5, including universal pre-K statewide and $4.5 billion in FY27 child care and pre-K funding (January 2026).
https://www.audacy.com/wben/news/state/gov-hochul-invests-to-deliver-universal-child-care-for-new-york-children-under-age-5
Says Trump's tariffs drive up grocery prices and that ending them would lower costs.
https://www.fox5ny.com/news/hochul-blakeman-debate-ny-governor-race

background: Chair of Queens Community Board 12 from December 2012 to November 2017.
Elected to the NYC Council for District 28 in November 2017.
Elected NYC Council Speaker in January 2022, the first Black woman in the post; finished fourth in the 2025 Democratic mayoral primary.
Before public office, worked in corporate executive training at firms including Goldman Sachs, Merrill Lynch and Revlon.
positions: Lists affordable housing, child care and lowering costs as her priorities.
https://abc7ny.com/post/governor-kathy-hochul-taps-former-new-york-city-council-speaker-adrienne-adams-running-mate/18541929/
Says the campaign will focus on affordable housing, wages and community safety.
https://www.fingerlakes1.com/2026/09/16/working-families-party-endorses-hochul-for-reelection/
Says Trump administration policies raise costs and cut child care for New York families.
https://queenseagle.com/all/2026/2/5/former-queens-lawmaker-to-run-as-hochuls-lieutenant-governor
endorsements: New York Democrats, at an August 2026 event with Rep. Yvette Clarke and Council Member Rita Joseph

background: Lost the 1998 race for State Comptroller to Carl McCall; Gov. George Pataki appointed him a Port Authority commissioner, and he served until 2009.
Former Presiding Officer of the Nassau County Legislature; Hempstead Town Councilman, 2015 to 2021.
